description:
Seven tests excluded from the default suite assert nothing, and their exclusion is recorded as if it were a cost decision.

## Background

`cargo nextest run --workspace --run-ignored ignored-only` at `cb8d42c3` runs all seven in 0.317 s combined, the slowest at 308 ms:

    test_validate_branch_drift_detects_drifted_branch   6 ms
    lock_tests::test_lock_released_on_drop              7 ms
    lock_tests::test_try_lock_non_blocking              7 ms
    lock_tests::test_exclusive_lock_prevents_concurrent_writes  7 ms
    lock_tests::test_shared_locks_allow_concurrent_reads        7 ms
    lock_tests::test_exclusive_lock_blocks_shared_locks       209 ms
    lock_tests::test_timeout_on_lock_contention               308 ms

They are fast because they exercise nothing. The six in `crates/jit/tests/fast_docs_templates/lock_tests.rs` are TDD placeholders whose real bodies are commented out and whose assertions are satisfied by the placeholder that replaced them:

    // TODO: Use FileLocker once implemented
    // let locker = FileLocker::new(Duration::from_millis(100));
    // if let Ok(_guard) = locker.lock_exclusive(&_path) { ... }

    // For now, placeholder
    if i == 0 { *success_count.lock().unwrap() += 1; }
    ...
    assert_eq!(count, 1, "Only one thread should acquire exclusive lock");

The assertion passes because the placeholder increments a counter for thread 0. It tests an `if`. Their stated removal condition — `#[ignore] // Remove once FileLocker is implemented` — was met: `lock_exclusive` is live in `crates/jit/src/storage/claim_coordinator.rs` and four other modules.

The seventh, `worktree_cli_tests::test_validate_branch_drift_detects_drifted_branch`, has an empty body and a comment stating that real coverage would need a remote repository.

A passing `#[ignore]`d test that proves nothing is worse than no test: it occupies the name of a property nobody is checking, and `--run-ignored` reports it green.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Every one of the seven is either given a body that proves the property its name claims, or deleted with the reason recorded. A placeholder assertion that passes on its own scaffolding does not satisfy this.
- [hard] REQ-02: For each one implemented rather than deleted, the test runs in the default suite unless there is a stated reason it cannot, and that reason is a property of the test rather than of its unfinished state.
- [hard] REQ-03: `dev/TESTING.md`'s account of the excluded set matches what remains after this change.
- [hard] REQ-04: The full workspace suite passes, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` is clean, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` reports zero warnings.

## Notes

File locking behaviour is already covered elsewhere — `storage::claim_coordinator` carries property-based concurrency tests (`prop_concurrent_claims_exclusive`, `prop_concurrent_different_issues_succeed`). Establish what those already prove before writing anything new; the honest outcome for some or all six may be deletion rather than implementation, per `@/inv/canonical-cutover`.

Found while measuring the excluded set for `76ecc11f`, which documents it. The measurement is in that issue's evidence.
title: Seven ignored tests assert nothing and are recorded as an excluded cost
